A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLM-wrapper and contain matching methods and overlapping experiments. Their substantive text, tables and figures are readable. v1 has no appendix; v3's Appendices A–E are available and included in this comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RefCOCOg experiments, including adaptation, ensembling, cross-VLM transfer and training dynamics in Section 3, Tables 1–3 and Figure 2.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds multi-dataset evaluations, segmentation results, sensitivity studies and failure analyses in Section 4 and Appendices A–E.

M1.justification: The central procedure remains a frozen VLM followed by a LoRA-trained LLM selecting a box from textualized detections. Appendix B adds a SAM box-to-mask conversion stage for referring-expression segmentation, a limited extension of the output pipeline.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates REC only on RefCOCOg. v3 adds RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, the driving-domain Talk2Car dataset and long-expression HC-RefLoCo, including evaluation without target-dataset training. Appendix B also adds referring-expression segmentation on RefCOCOg, substantially broadening domain and task coverage.

E2.justification: The original GD, GDrec and Florence-2 comparisons remain. v3 adds Kosmos-2 and a Contrastive Region Guidance comparison in Table 8, plus LISA-7B FT and GLaMM in the segmentation comparison of Table 9. CRG, LISA and GLaMM scores are explicitly imported from cited papers, rather than reported as new replications.

E3.justification: v3 introduces cross-dataset transfer protocols, cIoU/gIoU segmentation evaluation, additional LLM configurations and systematic hyperparameter controls. Existing settings are also reported differently: GD's confidence threshold changes from 0.15 to 0.2, Florence-2's listed detection mode changes from object detection to open vocabulary detection, and training changes from a stated single epoch to training until convergence. These textual revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ensembling, cross-VLM transfer and training-dynamics analyses, v3 adds cross-dataset generalization tests, adaptation of already REC-tuned models, and ablations on LLM scale, LoRA rank and learning rate. Appendices C–E add parameter/reasoning correlations, input-complexity breakdowns, invalid-output analysis and substantially expanded qualitative failure studies.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 and Table 11 introduce Pearson-correlation estimation between REC performance and model size, trainable parameters, MMLU and HellaSwag scores. This adds a statistical analysis absent from v1. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive dataset-transfer, segmentation and ablation results. Original GD/GDrec RefCOCOg entries and ensemble scores are retained, but Florence-2 results are revised: baseline validation/test P@1 changes from 68.28/66.90 to 67.91/66.16, and Llama3-wrapped scores from 77.94/77.15 to 78.76/78.03. Because Florence-2 settings also change, these are revised reports, not established same-setting gains. The GD-1.5 zero-shot-LLM score of 59.00 is retained in v3 Table 7.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, assumptions, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations. v3's explanations of standard evaluation metrics and input-complexity counts document empirical analyses without introducing a new theoretical development.

C1.justification: The central claims of black-box adaptation, ensembling and cross-VLM transfer remain. v3 extends the contribution with an explicit cross-dataset generalization claim and qualifies the competitive-performance framing: its abstract and introduction state that LLM-wrapper is not intended to outperform standard white-box fine-tuning.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of dataset-dependent gains, complementary VLM precision/recall, and the relationship between pretrained reasoning ability and adaptation performance. It explains degradation with repeated box labels and additional failure mechanisms involving missing candidates, context or labels. New limitations include added inference cost and dependence on SAM for segmentation; the original missing-visual-cues limitation remains.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v3 states that code and checkpoints are available and supplies a repository link. v3 additionally documents Adam, the default learning rate, trainable-parameter counts, IoU-based training-sample filtering, randomized proposal ordering, invalid-index fallback and training time. These materially improve documentation without establishing that newly disclosed implementation choices were introduced after v1.

R1.justification: v1's brief introductory positioning becomes a dedicated Related Work section in v3. It substantially expands comparisons with feature-access methods, black-box prompt tuning, image-input adaptation and CRG, explaining differences in access requirements and inference calls. New discussions also cover DoRA, VeRA, prefix tuning and segmentation-specific models.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, and the method exposition is reorganized into general idea, prompt construction and fine-tuning subsections. Experiments are restructured around adaptation, benefits and ablations, with dedicated related work and organized appendices. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the addition of experimental content.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column formatting to a single-column conference layout. Figure 1 is redrawn to expose the prompt-processing pipeline, while its white-box comparison becomes Table 1. Result tables expand and new plots and qualitative panels appear. Existing material is also redistributed, including the training curve from v1 Figure 2 to v3 Figure 5.

improvement.justification: v1's generality claims rested largely on one dataset. v3 substantially strengthens that evidence through broader domains, cross-dataset transfer, systematic sensitivity studies and detailed failure analysis. Clearer positioning and expanded implementation and access information also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh remaining limitations: repeated-run uncertainty is still absent, and Table 8's CRG comparison uses different starting baseline scores, weakening its direct superiority claim.
